Chapter 9. The Wisdom of Choosing Allies and Avoiding Fools.
You know, nobody really makes it on their own. Every step of your journey is shaped by the people who walk beside you—friends, mentors, coworkers, and sometimes even rivals.
Most of us have, at some point, found ourselves tangled up with folks who just seem to drain our energy or steer us in the wrong direction. But the truly wise? They learn to pick their companions with care.
Let me share a story. Imagine a project that started with promise, but it stumbled—not because the team lacked skill, but because conflict kept bubbling up. There was one person who always saw the negative, spreading doubt and division wherever they went. But then there was someone else, the encourager, who lifted everyone’s spirits and helped people shine.
It became clear: the company you keep shapes not just what you achieve, but who you become.
Most of us don’t realize just how much we absorb from those around us—their attitudes, their habits, the way they look at the world. The wise? They’re intentional about it. They look for people who push them to grow, who give honest feedback, and who genuinely cheer for their success—with no jealousy attached.
There’s also a real wisdom in steering clear of fools. And I’m not just talking about people who don’t know something, but those who refuse to learn, who seem to thrive on chaos, or who can’t be trusted. The wise set boundaries—not out of pride, but to protect their own energy. They know their time is precious, and not every relationship is worth the cost.
Now, picking allies doesn’t mean looking for perfect people—nobody’s flawless. It’s about finding those whose values line up with yours, whose strengths make up for your weaknesses, and whose presence brings out your best. Over time, these relationships become a wellspring of strength, resilience, and real joy.
